definition: Swelling confined to the bitten segment of the limb
Swelling spreading beyond the bitten segment (e.g. more than half the limb)
Blisters or bullae near the bite site
Tissue necrosis at or around the bite site
Tender enlarged lymph nodes draining the bitten limb
Incoagulable blood (positive 20-minute whole blood clotting test) or laboratory coagulopathy
Spontaneous systemic bleeding (gums, haematuria, haematemesis, other sites)
Acute kidney injury (oliguria or rising creatinine)
Difficulty swallowing or speaking, pooling of secretions
